_note: How many job seekers near this posting are looking for this kind of work (Tushar, 2026-10-23: tell the employer how many matching candidates there are, never who). signals-search over seeker profiles, anchored on the employer's own job posting, narrowed by the role words, within 20 km of the posting. Only message.meta.total is used; names come back masked and are never spoken. Probes 2026-10-23: gzb machine operator 175, electrician 387, helper 8; dwd fitter 846-864. A combined role ('Electrician | Fitter') returns 0 because every word must match, so the role is ONE kind of work. Headers cloned from create_job (x-acting-org-id dropped), so no key is stored in this repo.
name: get_candidate_count
description: How many job seekers within 20 km of this job are looking for this kind of work. Call it right after create_job returned the posted item, before you speak. job_id = the item_id of the posting create_job returned; role = ONE kind of work in plain English ("machine operator", "helper"), never two roles and never a '|'. Read only message.meta.total. The result also carries masked profile fields: never speak a name, age, place or any other detail from it.

job_id.description: The item_id of the job posting create_job just returned (a UUID). Exactly the item_id from get_employer or create_job, nothing added before or after it (no comma, no space).

role.description: ONE kind of work in plain English words, e.g. "machine operator". No '|', no second role, no place.
